partners.mechanism_chain: CDH1 (HGNC:2106) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837); Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837) —LEADS_TO→ Endometrial cancer (MONDO:0011962); HSPG2 (HGNC:4986) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Silverman-Handmaker type dyssegmental dysplasia (MONDO:0009140); Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837) —BINDS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198). Loss-of-function mutations in CDH1 disrupt epithelial cell adhesion, promoting epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) which is a key driver of endometrial cancer. Separately, loss-of-function mutations in HSPG2 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to skeletal and connective tissue abnormalities characteristic of Silverman-Handmaker type dyssegmental dysplasia. The hypothesized convergence is that dysregulation of extracellular matrix organization (via HSPG2) can indirectly influence cell-cell adhesion and signaling pathways involved in EMT (via CDH1), creating a shared regulatory space that, when perturbed by distinct genetic defects, results in these disparate disease phenotypes.
